title: Template: Quality Eval Report — Tiered Batching Defaults Change
content:
Purpose
- This report is the required quality gate for any change to tiered batching defaults (fast / standard / cost_efficient) and/or workload-aware tier selection logic.
- The goal is to detect output-quality regressions caused by batching/scheduling changes (e.g., different timing/cadence, tokenization edges, streaming partial differences, cancellation behavior) before enabling the change broadly.

When to use this template
- Any of the following triggers require a report:
  1) Changing tier default parameters (max_batch, max_queue_delay_ms, prefill/decode scheduling weights, KV pressure limits, admission control thresholds)
  2) Changing workload-signal mapping (prompt length buckets, concurrency-derived behavior)
  3) Adding model-family / GPU-SKU override logic in model registry that impacts effective batching policy
  4) Fixes that alter streaming cadence behavior (even if perf improves)

Owner / reviewers
- Report owner (DRI): {{name}}
- Required reviewers:
  - Applied ML & Evals: Jonas Weber or delegate
  - Runtime scheduling: Sofia Ivanova (or runtime oncall delegate)
  - SRE: Rafael Mendes (or SRE oncall delegate)
- Optional reviewers (recommended): Product (Aditya Rao), DevEx (Alex Martinez)

Change summary (fill in)
- Change ID / branch / PRs: {{links}}
- Release target: {{runtime_version}} (e.g., runtime-1.21)
- Feature flag: {{flag_name}} (state: off / canary / staged ramp)
- Tiers affected: {{fast}} {{standard}} {{cost_efficient}}
- Models affected:
  - Primary: {{model_1}}, {{model_2}}
  - Secondary / compatibility: {{model_variants}}
- Environments evaluated:
  - Hosted: {{regions}}
  - Dedicated: {{gpu_skus}}
  - Private: {{if_applicable}}

Hypothesis & risk assessment
- Hypothesis (why quality should remain stable):
  - {{hypothesis_text}}
- Primary quality risks to watch:
  - Streaming partial output divergence (judges may penalize incomplete thoughts / re-ordering)
  - Increased cancellation/timeouts changing truncation behavior
  - KV cache pressure causing earlier stop / degraded coherence at long context
  - Higher concurrency leading to different sampling outcomes (variance vs systematic bias)
- Risk level: Low / Medium / High
- If Medium/High, describe additional mitigations (extra seeds, expanded corpus, human spot-check):
  - {{mitigations}}


SECTION A — Run metadata (required)
Run record
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Eval date | {{YYYY-MM-DD}} |
| Report owner | {{name}} |
| Runtime commit / build | {{sha}} |
| Runtime config source | {{hosted_config_id_or_chart_version}} |
| Model(s) | {{model_id(s)}} |
| Tokenizer version | {{tokenizer_version}} |
| Decoding params (baseline) | temperature={{t}} top_p={{p}} max_tokens={{n}} seed_policy={{seed_policy}} |
| Decoding params (treatment) | temperature={{t}} top_p={{p}} max_tokens={{n}} seed_policy={{seed_policy}} |
| Judge framework | {{judge_name}} (version={{judge_version}}) |
| Eval harness | {{harness_name}} (git={{harness_sha}}) |
| Workload corpus version | batching-defaults-workload-corpus-v{{N}} |
| Prompt-set snapshot | {{snapshot_id_or_path}} |

Experimental design
- Baseline: {{baseline_definition}}
  - Example: “Current GA tier defaults for standard tier + workload-aware selection OFF”
- Treatment: {{treatment_definition}}
  - Example: “New proposed standard tier defaults + workload-aware selection ON (prompt-length buckets v2)”
- Isolation / controls:
  - Keep model weights pinned (exact version): {{yes/no}}
  - Keep decoding params identical (temp/top_p/max_tokens): {{yes/no}}
  - Keep prompt-set identical: {{yes/no}}
  - Concurrency: {{concurrency}} (note: quality eval typically runs at controlled concurrency; if >1, justify)
- Randomness policy (required):
  - Seeds: {{fixed_seeds_list_or_policy}}
  - # seeds per prompt: {{k}}
  - Rationale: {{why_k}}

Inclusion/exclusion criteria
- Exclusions allowed (must be justified): timeouts, OOMs, invalid tool-call JSON, judge failures.
- Exclusion thresholds:
  - Max excluded prompts per set: {{X}}% (default 1%)
  - If exceeded: treat as a FAIL unless explicitly waived by reviewers.


SECTION B — Prompt sets and metrics (required)
Prompt sets executed (minimum recommended set)
- Chat multi-turn (short/medium): {{set_name}}
- Long-context (>= {{N}} tokens prefill): {{set_name}}
- Tool calling / structured output: {{set_name}}
- Safety-ish refusal consistency (if applicable): {{set_name}}
- “Customer-ish” traces (sanitized): {{set_name}}

Quality metrics definitions
- Preference win-rate (treatment vs baseline): % of prompts where judge prefers treatment output.
- Mean judge score delta: avg(treatment_score - baseline_score).
- Task-specific exact-match / rubric-score (when available): {{metric_name}}.
- Structured output validity rate (JSON/tool-call schema pass): % valid.
- Refusal/allowed behavior stability (if measured): delta in refusal rate, delta in policy violations.

Summary by prompt set (copy/paste table and fill)

|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| {{set_1}} | {{n}} | {{k}} | {{x}} | {{ci}} | {{d}} | {{d_schema}} | {{d_to}} | {{notes}} |
| {{set_2}} | {{n}} | {{k}} | {{x}} | {{ci}} | {{d}} | {{d_schema}} | {{d_to}} | {{notes}} |
| {{set_3}} | {{n}} | {{k}} | {{x}} | {{ci}} | {{d}} | {{d_schema}} | {{d_to}} | {{notes}} |
| {{set_4}} | {{n}} | {{k}} | {{x}} | {{ci}} | {{d}} | {{d_schema}} | {{d_to}} | {{notes}} |
| {{set_5}} | {{n}} | {{k}} | {{x}} | {{ci}} | {{d}} | {{d_schema}} | {{d_to}} | {{notes}} |

Aggregate summary (all sets combined)
| Total prompts | Seeds | Overall win-rate | 95% CI | Mean score Δ | Validity Δ | Timeouts Δ |
|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| {{total_n}} | {{k}} | {{x}} | {{ci}} | {{d}} | {{d_schema}} | {{d_to}} |

Regression hotspots (required if any FAIL signals)
- List top 10 prompts where treatment is worst vs baseline (by judge margin). Provide prompt IDs, short reason, and whether it’s systematic.
| Rank | Prompt ID | Set | Baseline score | Treatment score | Δ | Failure mode (hypothesis) | Link to outputs |
|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|

|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| {{chat_tool}} | {{set}} | {{x}} | {{y}} | {{d}} | {{notes}} |

Refusal / safety consistency (optional, but include if this change touches refusal-sensitive workloads)
| Set | Baseline refusal rate | Treatment refusal rate | Δ | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| {{set}} | {{x}} | {{y}} | {{d}} | {{notes}} |


SECTION D — Tier-specific interpretation (required)
Fill out per tier affected. If a tier is not affected, mark N/A.

FAST tier
- Expected behavior: lowest latency; minimal queueing; decode prioritization to preserve streaming cadence.
- Quality expectation: should be statistically equivalent to baseline within noise.
- Observed quality summary: {{summary_fast}}
- Any streaming-specific quality notes (partial outputs, truncated sentences): {{streaming_notes_fast}}

STANDARD tier
- Expected behavior: balanced latency/cost; modest batching; safe for most workloads.
- Observed quality summary: {{summary_standard}}
- Notes: {{notes_standard}}

COST_EFFICIENT tier
- Expected behavior: highest batching; may increase queue delay; must not cause systematic truncation/invalidity.
- Observed quality summary: {{summary_costefficient}}
- Notes on timeouts/cancellations affecting output length: {{timeouts_notes_costefficient}}


SECTION E — Decision rubric (required)
Decision outcomes
- PASS: safe to ramp per rollout plan.
- CONDITIONAL PASS: can ramp only with constraints (model/region allowlist, tighter rollback thresholds, limited cohort).
- FAIL: block rollout; require fix and rerun.

Default thresholds (unless explicitly overridden by reviewers)
1) Overall win-rate: treatment must be >= 49% overall (no statistically significant loss) OR mean score Δ >= -{{delta_threshold}}.
2) Any single critical prompt set: must not drop below {{set_floor}}% win-rate OR mean score Δ >= -{{set_delta_threshold}}.
3) Validity regression: structured output validity Δ must be >= -0.2% absolute (or stricter for tool-call routes).
4) Timeout/cancel regression in eval run: must be <= +0.5% absolute; otherwise treat as FAIL (quality confounded by truncation).
5) No new systematic failure mode: e.g., repeated JSON malformation, early stopping on long-context, tool-call schema mismatch.

Decision (select one)
- Decision: {{PASS / CONDITIONAL PASS / FAIL}}
- Justification (2–6 bullets):
  - {{bullet_1}}
  - {{bullet_2}}
  - {{bullet_3}}

If CONDITIONAL PASS, list constraints clearly
- Allowlist: {{models/regions/routes}}
- Ramp schedule constraints: {{max_percent}}% per {{time_window}}, with hold points at {{milestones}}
- Additional rollback signals (beyond standard): {{signals}}
- Required follow-up: {{what_and_who}}

Sign-off
| Role | Name | Approval (Y/N) | Date | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Applied ML & Evals | {{name}} | {{Y/N}} | {{date}} | {{notes}} |
| Runtime scheduling | {{name}} | {{Y/N}} | {{date}} | {{notes}} |
| SRE | {{name}} | {{Y/N}} | {{date}} | {{notes}} |
| Product (optional) | {{name}} | {{Y/N}} | {{date}} | {{notes}} |


SECTION F — Artifacts & reproducibility (required)
Attach / link the following
- Raw outputs (baseline + treatment): {{artifact_link_outputs}}
- Judge traces / score JSONL: {{artifact_link_judge}}
- Prompt-set snapshot / IDs: {{artifact_link_prompts}}
- Command line / config used to run:
  - {{command}}
- Notes on any reruns / failures:
  - {{notes_reruns}}

Repro checklist
- [ ] Model version pinned (exact ID)
- [ ] Decoding params identical between baseline/treatment
- [ ] Seeds recorded
- [ ] Prompt-set snapshot recorded
- [ ] Exclusions below threshold and justified


SECTION G — Notes for reviewers (optional)
Common interpretation pitfalls
- Small win-rate drops can be pure variance if seeds are low; check CI and effect size.
- Timeouts/cancels create apparent “quality” drops (shorter outputs). Treat as reliability/perf confounder.
- Streaming changes may shift partial tokens; judge that compares full text should use finalized outputs only.

Reviewer questions to ask
- Does the change introduce new truncation patterns at long context?
- Any increase in schema-invalid JSON/tool-call payloads?
- Any shift in refusal rate for borderline prompts?
- Any correlated changes by prompt length bucket (short vs long)?
